answer: An agent marketplace requires every active identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs. Agents such as basalt, atlas, and opal each need a separate bond, and one bond cannot back multiple identities at once. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up $100,000 for a month, even if no fraud is detected. This does not prove identities are unique; it makes a swarm costly by forcing the attacker to commit scarce capital for every account.
